title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Swell rebuilds after an October wipeout
conditions.summary: Futures are bouncing, led by the Nasdaq, after tech's worst month since March 2025, while crude slides on US-Iran talk hopes. Apple and Palantir report tonight, with midterms Tuesday and the jobs report Friday.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.9% in early trading (quotes from roughly 5:15–5:40 AM ET).
Dow futures are up about 0.5% and Russell 2000 futures about 0.8%.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to 4.93%; no fresh dollar index reading was found this morning.
WTI crude slid about 4.5% to near $99 and Brent to near $109 on hopes for Qatar-mediated US-Iran talks.
Gold rose 0.4% to about $3,913; bitcoin is flat near $77,800 after a $6.3 billion hack at Binance; the VIX eased to about 18.9.
Asia was mixed: mainland China and Korea rallied while Japan's Topix slipped; Europe opened slightly higher, helped by firm UK factory data.
Backdrop: the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.2% in October, its worst month since March 2025, on worries about AI spending.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 9:00 AM CT: ISM Manufacturing for October, consensus 54.7 vs 54.5 prior; prices paid seen at 77.5.
9:00 AM CT: Construction spending for September, consensus +0.5% m/m.
The S&P Global final October manufacturing PMI is also due; the flash reading was 56.0.
The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28 in a 10-2 vote; the next meeting is Dec. 9.
US midterm elections are Tuesday; the main macro story remains doubts about AI spending after big-tech earnings.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Last week Alphabet fell about 13% after a miss, Amazon sold off after a double miss, and Intel dropped more than 28% on a weak forecast.
Apple reports after today's close; consensus EPS is about $1.98, and the focus is iPhone sales, Services, margins and guidance.
Palantir reports after the close; consensus EPS is about $0.33, with watchers eyeing commercial and government growth.
Vertex, ON Semiconductor, Roku, Realty Income and Super Micro are also slated after the close.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: OKTA (Okta): +3.6% — set to join the S&P 500, replacing Kenvue.
AAPL (Apple): −0.4% — slipping ahead of tonight's earnings.
INTC (Intel): +0.2% — steadying after last week's 28% plunge.
SPCX (SpaceX): higher — among early gainers; reportedly in talks over Boost Mobile's network.
GOOGL (Alphabet): higher — rebounding after last week's 13% earnings drop.
Pre-market quotes are early and thin; percentages for several movers were not available.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic has publicly filed for an IPO.
OpenAI reportedly cut the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion.
Binance was hit by a hack of about $6.3 billion, described as the biggest crypto theft yet.
Apollo launched a €10 billion European credit platform.
Washington Post reports SpaceX is in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 9:00 AM CT ISM Manufacturing: a reading above 54.7 would point to firm factory demand.
Whether the Nasdaq bounce holds after October's AI-driven sell-off.
Apple and Palantir after the close, around 4:00 PM CT, ahead of Tuesday's midterms.

sections.title: Earnings This Week
items: Mon: Apple (AAPL), after close — iPhone sales, Services, margins, holiday guidance.
Mon: Palantir (PLTR), after close — US commercial and government revenue, AIP adoption.
Tue: Shopify (SHOP), before open — e-commerce volume and payments.
Tue: Pfizer (PFE), before open — drug sales and full-year guidance.
Tue: AMD (AMD), after close — data center and AI accelerator demand.
Tue: Arista (ANET), after close — AI networking demand.
Wed: Uber (UBER), before open — gross bookings and trip volumes.
Wed: McDonald's (MCD), before open — same-store sales and consumer spending.
Wed: Qualcomm (QCOM), after close — handsets, autos and AI PCs.
Wed: Arm (ARM), after close — licensing, royalties and data center adoption.
Thu: ConocoPhillips (COP), before open — production, costs and capex.
Thu: Airbnb (ABNB), after close — booking trends and Q4 outlook.

sections.title: Economic Calendar This Week
items: Mon 9:00 AM CT: ISM Manufacturing (Oct) — consensus 54.7.
Tue: US midterm elections; 9:00 AM CT JOLTS job openings and factory orders (Sep).
Wed 7:15 AM CT: ADP employment (Oct); 7:30 AM CT trade balance (Sep).
Wed 9:00 AM CT: ISM Services (Oct) — consensus 54.7; Treasury quarterly refunding announcement also Wednesday.
Thu 7:30 AM CT: Jobless claims and Q3 productivity and unit labor costs; Bank of England decision.
Fri 7:30 AM CT: October jobs report — consensus +55,000, unemployment 4.2%; UMich sentiment also due.
No FOMC meeting this week (next is Dec. 9); clocks moved back Nov. 1, so CT is now ET minus one hour.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November second, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Gus the wonder dog just trotted in from his morning beach run with sand on his nose. Give the crew a big hello, Gus! [BARK]

Welcome to Dawn Patrol, and this is our week ahead edition. October was a gnarly month. The Nasdaq Composite fell about five percent, its worst month since March of last year, as doubts about A I spending knocked big tech off its board. This morning the swell is rebuilding. In early trading, S and P 500 futures are up about half a percent. Nasdaq 100 futures are up nearly nine tenths of a percent. Dow futures are up about half a percent, and Russell 2000 futures are up about eight tenths. The ten year Treasury yield slipped about six basis points to four point nine three percent. Crude oil dropped about four and a half percent to around ninety-nine dollars, on hopes for talks between the U S and Iran. Gold is up a bit. Bitcoin is flat near seventy-eight thousand dollars after a huge hack at the Binance exchange. The VIX fear gauge eased below nineteen. Overseas, mainland China stocks rallied, and Europe opened a touch higher.

On the weather map, the I S M manufacturing report lands at nine A M Central, with forecasts near fifty-four point seven. The Fed held rates steady last week, and its next meeting is December ninth. Tomorrow is Election Day for the midterms, so expect some choppy water.

On the tide chart, Apple and Palantir report after today's close. Apple is the big Kahuna of this week. Traders want to see iPhone sales, services, profit margins and next quarter's outlook. For Palantir, the focus is growth in commercial and government deals. Vertex also reports tonight.

In the lineup, Okta is up about three and a half percent before the bell after it was picked to join the S and P 500, replacing Kenvue. Now that's a stock catching a real wave. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK] Apple is down a little ahead of its numbers. Intel is steady after last week's wipeout, when it plunged more than twenty-eight percent. Early quotes are thin, so take them with a grain of sand.

Beach talk. Anthropic has filed publicly for its I P O, the grom everyone is watching. OpenAI reportedly trimmed its latest funding target by ten billion dollars. And Binance was hit by a hack of about six point three billion dollars, called the biggest crypto hack ever.

Now for the week's swell forecast. Tonight, Apple and Palantir. Tuesday, Shopify and Pfizer before the open, then A M D, Amgen, Arista and Booking Holdings after the close. Wednesday, Uber, McDonald's and C V S in the morning, with Qualcomm, Arm and AppLovin after the bell. Thursday, ConocoPhillips in the morning, then Airbnb and Cloudflare after the close. On the economy, job openings and factory orders arrive Tuesday at nine A M Central. Wednesday brings the A D P jobs report at seven fifteen A M Central, I S M services at nine, and the Treasury refunding announcement. Thursday has jobless claims at seven thirty. Friday at seven thirty A M Central brings the October jobs report, with forecasts near fifty-five thousand new jobs and a four point two percent unemployment rate. The two waves most likely to make a splash are the midterm results Tuesday night and Friday's jobs report. Soul surfers, stay patient through the chop.

This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
